_note: Films and series for /culture/films-et-series: title, year, maker and our own short description, nothing else. No streaming links (they change). `level` is our estimate of how much French you need to enjoy it with French subtitles. Years and makers are from memory of well-documented works and are listed 'to verify' in the culture report. Added 2026-11-12.

items.title: Intouchables
items.text: A rich man in a wheelchair hires a young man from the suburbs as his carer. A warm comedy with clear, everyday speech and a little street slang.

items.title: Le Fabuleux Destin d'Amélie Poulain
items.text: A shy waitress in Paris secretly makes small things better for the people around her. Gentle, visual and full of charm, with a narrator who speaks slowly.

items.title: Bienvenue chez les Ch'tis
items.text: A post office manager is sent from the south to the far north of France and expects the worst. The joke is the regional speech, so it teaches you how varied French can sound.

items.title: Les Choristes
items.text: A new supervisor at a boys' boarding school in 1949 starts a choir. Calm, clear French, and music that helps you follow the story.

items.title: La Famille Bélier
items.text: A teenage girl in a farming family is the only hearing person at home, and she is asked to leave for a singing school. Family life, with sign language and spoken French side by side.

items.title: Au revoir les enfants
items.text: At a boarding school in occupied France, a boy discovers that a new pupil is hiding a secret. A quiet, serious film with school language of the 1940s.

items.title: La Haine
items.text: Twenty-four hours in the lives of three friends in a Paris suburb after a night of unrest. Fast speech, slang and verlan; watch it with subtitles and read the dialogue.

items.title: Le Prénom
items.by: Alexandre de La Patellière and Matthieu Delaporte
items.text: A dinner among friends and family goes wrong when a man says what name he plans to give his child. Almost all of it is talk, so you hear natural, quick arguments.

items.title: Dix pour cent
items.text: The staff of a Paris talent agency look after film actors, who play themselves. Work French, jokes and fast dialogues in short episodes.

items.title: Le Bureau des légendes
items.text: A spy series about French agents who work abroad under false identities. Serious, precise language for work and politics, in the style of a thriller.

items.title: Monsieur Lazhar
items.text: A school in Montréal and an Algerian teacher who replaces a colleague after a tragedy. Clear Québec French in the classroom, calm and human.

items.title: La Grande Séduction
items.text: A small fishing village in Québec needs a doctor to get a factory, so the villagers try to charm the new one. A comedy with a strong Québec accent and local expressions.

items.title: Incendies
items.text: Twin sister and brother in Québec follow the past of their mother to the Middle East after her death. A heavy film with some violent scenes; the dialogue is slow and clear.

items.title: Rosetta
items.text: A young woman in a Belgian town fights to find and keep a job. Simple, short sentences, and a good example of Belgian French.

items.title: Le Gamin au vélo
items.text: A boy in Belgium, left by his father, finds a hairdresser who takes care of him. Short, everyday dialogues about family and trust.

items.title: La Noire de…
items.text: A young woman from Dakar goes to work for a French family on the Riviera. One of the first major films from sub-Saharan Africa, with a thoughtful voice-over and slow French.
